title: ORARE Registry: Open and Robot-Assisted Resection in Urachal Carcinoma – A Retrospective Multicenter Registry
summary:
Urachal carcinoma is a very rare cancer that develops from a small embryologic remnant located between the bladder and the umbilicus. Because this cancer is so uncommon, there are no large prospective studies and many aspects of treatment remain uncertain. In particular, it is still unclear how extensive surgery should be, whether the umbilicus always needs to be removed, when lymph nodes should be removed, and how open, laparoscopic, and robotic surgery perform in this disease.

The ORARE Registry will collect information from several hospitals on patients who were treated with open, laparoscopic, or robot-assisted surgery for urachal carcinoma. In the first phase, participating hospitals will retrospectively identify eligible patients who have already been treated and enter information that is already available in their medical records. After this initial phase, the registry is planned to continue prospectively, so that future patients treated with open, laparoscopic, or robot-assisted surgery for urachal carcinoma can also be documented over time.

The study will record information on symptoms, diagnostic tests, imaging, surgery, pathology results, molecular testing, additional treatments such as chemotherapy, cancer recurrence, metastases, and survival. The aim is to better understand how open, laparoscopic, and robotic surgery for urachal carcinoma is currently performed and which clinical, surgical, pathologic, and molecular factors may be associated with recurrence and survival.

The study does not change patient treatment and does not require any additional tests or visits beyond routine clinical care. Its purpose is to improve future research and help physicians make more informed decisions for patients with this rare cancer.

interventions.name: Patients with histologically confirmed urachal carcinoma who underwent open, laparoscopic, or robot-assisted resection with curative or cytoreductive intent.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed primary urachal carcinoma, including adenocarcinoma and other malignant urachal histologies, provided the diagnosis was classified as primary urachal carcinoma on overall clinicopathological assessment. Index surgery with oncologic resection of urachal carcinoma using open, laparoscopic, or robot-assisted technique between 01/01/2000 and the date of application submission. Availability of a minimum routine dataset (surgical approach, extent of resection, histopathologic diagnosis, margin status or documented reason for unavailability, and at least one follow-up or vital status parameter). Treatment at a participating center with local approval for pseudonymized data transfer to the coordinating center.
Exclusion criteria:
Benign urachal anomalies without histologically confirmed carcinoma. Secondary involvement of the urachus or bladder by an extravesical adenocarcinoma, in particular colorectal, gynecologic, or other metastatic adenocarcinoma, provided no primary urachal carcinoma is present. Primary non-urachal adenocarcinoma of the bladder without urachal origin. Diagnostic TUR-B or biopsy only, without open, laparoscopic, or robot-assisted oncologic resection. Lack of local authorization to use or transfer pseudonymized data.
